 Live .  9,792 viewing 9792 viewing Carrick's future as Man Utd manager to be decided on Wednesday
 Summary
 Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting on Wednesday 
 The meeting will be attended by owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in Monaco
 It comes after their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday which means United are in the Premier League's relegation zone 
 As it stands, Michael Carrick remains Manchester United head coach and is due to take training this morning , writes Simon Stone 
 Carrick arrived at training at 07:15 this morning 
 But there is a growing expectation that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend for Carrick to be sacked
 Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Mauricio Pochettino have all been linked with the position
 Close form Your views on Michael Carrick and Man Utd's future
 Get involved What information do we collect from this quiz? Live Reporting
 Written by Michael Emons, Marissa Thomas, Tasnim Chowdhury & Jemma Rice.

 Carrick's future to be decided on Wednesday published at 10:43 GMT 10:43 GMT Breaking 
 Dan Roan 
BBC sports editor 
 Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting attended by owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday
 Carrick’s position is under threat after the club slipped to 18th in the Premier League following a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.
 BBC Sport reported on Monday night that there is a growing expectation that chief executive Berrada and director of football Wilcox will recommend to minority owner Ratcliffe and the Glazer family for Carrick to be sacked.
 Berrada and Wilcox will present their recommendation and a decision on Carrick's future may not come until Thursday.

 Carrick taking Manchester United training published at 10:29 GMT 10:29 GMT 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter 
 As it stands, Michael Carrick remains Manchester United head coach and is due to take training this morning.
 He arrived at Carrington as normal and neither he nor his coaches have been told their services are no longer required.
 It is one of the weird issues around the football industry that word around decisions tends to leak out before they are communicated to those involved.
 This tends to be because of conversations that need to take place around potential replacements, and that tends to find its way into the media.
 Officially, Manchester United's hierarchy are still considering the situation with the recommendations of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox due to be communicated to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
 If a change is made as expected, it would be the third season in succession Manchester United had backed a manager in the summer, given them transfer funds, then sacked them in mid-season.

 Man Utd expected to sack head coach Carrick published at 09:19 GMT 09:19 GMT 
 Sami Mokbel and Simon Stone 
 Manchester United look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick.
 The club opted to stick with Carrick after the side's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, with the intention of reassessing the situation during this month's international break.
 Multiple sources have told BBC Sport that the board remain committed to that process, and that no final decision on Carrick's future has been made.
 However, there is a growing expectation that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family for Carrick to be sacked.
 The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.
